- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.
- 세부 기술 힌트: 삽입구·동격·긴 수식어 뒤에서 절 경계(콜론/대시/세미콜론/쉼표+등위접속사)를 판단하거나, 필수/비필수 수식어 쉼표를 가리는 문제. 선택지는 문장부호/접속 조합 4개.

g.passage: The bdelloid rotifer, a microscopic freshwater animal that has reproduced without males for tens of millions of years, survives drought by drying out completely and entering a dormant state known as anhydrobiosis. Geneticists sequencing the animal's genome noticed something unexpected about its DNA______ roughly ten percent of its active genes appear to have been acquired directly from bacteria, fungi, and plants.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.design: 첫 문장의 긴 동격구로 주의를 분산시키고, 빈칸 앞뒤가 모두 독립절임을 확인한 뒤 뒤 절이 앞의 'something unexpected'를 구체화한다는 문맥까지 연결해야 콜론을 고를 수 있게 했다.
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞 'Geneticists ... about its DNA'와 뒤 'roughly ten percent ... plants'는 각각 독립절이며, 뒤 절은 앞의 'something unexpected'가 무엇인지 구체적으로 설명합니다. 따라서 독립절 뒤에서 설명을 이끄는 콜론을 쓴 A가 정답입니다. B는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 콤마 스플라이스가 됩니다. C는 'that'이 DNA를 꾸미는 관계절처럼 보이지만 뒤 절에 빈자리가 없어 문법적으로 성립하지 않습니다. D는 문장부호 없이 두 독립절을 붙인 무종지문(run-on)입니다.
g.explanation_en: The text before the blank ("Geneticists ... about its DNA") and the text after it ("roughly ten percent ... plants") are both independent clauses, and the second clause explains what the "something unexpected" is. A colon is the right mark for introducing that kind of explanation after a complete clause, so A is correct. B joins two independent clauses with only a comma, which makes a comma splice. C might look like it starts a relative clause describing "DNA," but the clause after the blank isn't missing anything, so "that" doesn't fit grammatically. D runs the two independent clauses together with no punctuation, which makes a run-on sentence.

g.passage: In Lena Okafor's novel The Lamplighter's Debt, the house at Wrenfield has stood empty for eleven winters. Its last tenant—a retired ship's surgeon who, according to village gossip, kept a drowned sailor's compass on his mantel______ behind nothing but a ledger of unpaid debts and a single unopened letter addressed to his daughter.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: "tenant" 뒤에서 대시로 시작한 동격 삽입구(a retired ship's surgeon ... mantel)는 대시로 닫아야 하고, 그 뒤에 주어 "Its last tenant"의 동사 "had left"가 와야 한다. 따라서 B가 정답이다. A는 쉼표로 삽입구를 닫아 여는 대시와 짝이 맞지 않는다. C의 세미콜론은 주어와 동사를 갈라 놓아 앞부분이 독립절이 되지 못한다. D는 삽입구를 닫지 않아 "had left"가 관계절 "who ... kept"에 이어지는 것처럼 읽혀 주절의 동사가 사라진다.
g.explanation_en: The dash after "tenant" opens an appositive (a retired ship's surgeon ... on his mantel), so a second dash has to close it. After that comes "had left," the verb for the subject "Its last tenant." That makes B correct. A closes the appositive with a comma, which doesn't match the opening dash. C puts a semicolon between the subject and its verb, and a semicolon should join two independent clauses, but the text before it isn't one. D never closes the appositive, so "had left" reads as part of the "who ... kept" clause, and the main clause is left with no verb.
g.design: 긴 동격 삽입구와 그 안의 관계절·삽입절 뒤에서 대시를 짝 맞춰 닫는 문제다. 쉼표 오답은 삽입구 경계라는 점에서는 그럴듯하고, 문장부호 없는 오답은 관계절이 이어지는 것처럼 읽힌다.

g.passage: The Okavango Delta in northern Botswana, unlike most of the world's river deltas, never reaches the sea; its waters fan out across the Kalahari Basin and eventually evaporate or sink into the sand. Floodwaters that originate as rain in the Angolan highlands take roughly four months to travel through the delta's maze of channels ______ the flood typically peaks in July, well after the local rainy season has ended.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "Floodwaters ... take roughly four months to travel through the delta's maze of channels"와 빈칸 뒤 "the flood typically peaks in July ..."는 각각 독립절이다. 따라서 접속부사 "as a result" 앞에는 세미콜론이 와야 하고, 그 뒤에는 쉼표가 와야 한다. 그러므로 C가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 오류(comma splice)가 되고, B는 두 절 사이에 아무 문장부호도 없어 무종지문(run-on)이 된다. D는 세미콜론의 위치가 잘못되어 "as a result"가 앞 절에 붙게 되므로, 앞 절이 스스로의 결과라는 비논리적인 의미가 된다.
g.explanation_en: The text before the blank ("Floodwaters ... take roughly four months to travel through the delta's maze of channels") and the text after it ("the flood typically peaks in July ...") are both independent clauses. When a conjunctive adverb like "as a result" joins two independent clauses, it needs a semicolon before it and a comma after it, so C is correct. A connects the two independent clauses with only commas, which creates a comma splice. B has no punctuation between the clauses at all, which makes a run-on sentence. D puts the semicolon in the wrong place, attaching "as a result" to the first clause, so the first clause would illogically be presented as its own result.
g.design: The blank comes after a long first clause that includes a prepositional phrase. Students have to recognize that two independent clauses meet at the blank and that the transition can only sit correctly after a semicolon. The wrong options each get part of the punctuation right.

g.passage: By 1848 most British railway companies had adopted Greenwich Mean Time for their timetables, abandoning the local solar times that had differed from town to town. Not every community welcomed the change. The cathedral city of Exeter, whose clocks ran about fourteen minutes behind those of London______ held out until 1852, when the cathedral's dean finally agreed to reset its great clock.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 주어 "The cathedral city of Exeter" 뒤에 쉼표로 시작하는 비필수 관계절 "whose clocks ran ... London"이 삽입되었으므로, 이 관계절을 닫는 것도 쉼표여야 하고 그 뒤에 동사 "held out"이 이어진다. 따라서 D가 정답이다. A는 세미콜론 앞부분이 동사 없는 주어+수식어뿐이라 독립절이 아니며, 'it'이 주어를 중복시킨다. B는 ', and it'으로 새 절을 잇는 것처럼 보이지만 앞부분에 본동사가 없어 문장이 성립하지 않는다. C의 대시는 쉼표로 열린 삽입절을 닫을 수 없어 문장부호가 짝이 맞지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The subject "The cathedral city of Exeter" is followed by a nonessential relative clause that opens with a comma ("whose clocks ran ... London"), so that clause has to close with a comma too, and then the main verb "held out" follows. That makes D correct. A doesn't work because everything before the semicolon is just a subject plus a modifier, which isn't an independent clause, and "it" repeats the subject. B looks like it's joining two clauses, but the part before "and" has no main verb, so the sentence falls apart. C is wrong because a dash can't close an interruption that began with a comma; the punctuation has to match.
g.design: A long nonessential relative clause separates the subject from its verb. Students have to spot the opening comma and confirm that the part before the blank isn't a full clause before they can rule out the semicolon and conjunction choices, which look like clause joiners.

g.passage: In 2019, engineers at a Dutch startup tested a new kind of bicycle path built from recycled plastic bottles, a material chosen partly because it weighs far less than ______ the hollow modules could be assembled off-site and lowered into place in a single afternoon, sparing commuters weeks of detours.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.design: 긴 동격 수식어 뒤에서 두 독립절의 경계를 판단해야 하며, 접속부사 'as a result'가 어느 절에 속하는지 문맥으로 확인하는 두 단계 판단을 요구한다.
g.explanation: 'In 2019 ... weighs far less than asphalt'는 하나의 독립절이고, 'the hollow modules could be assembled...'도 독립절이므로 두 절 사이에 강한 경계가 필요하다. 'as a result'는 앞 내용(가벼움)의 결과로 조립이 가능했다는 뒤 절을 이끄는 접속부사이므로 세미콜론 뒤에 오고 쉼표가 따라야 한다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B와 D는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 무종지문(comma splice)이 된다. C는 세미콜론 위치는 그럴듯하지만 'as a result'를 앞 절에 붙여 무게가 가벼운 것이 결과인 것처럼 논리를 뒤집는다.
g.explanation_en: The text contains two independent clauses: one ending with "weighs far less than asphalt" and one beginning with "the hollow modules could be assembled." These need a strong boundary between them. "As a result" introduces the second clause, since the modules could be assembled off-site because the material is light. So it belongs after a semicolon and should be followed by a comma, which makes A correct. B and D join two independent clauses with only commas, so they create comma splices. C uses a semicolon, but it attaches "as a result" to the first clause, which wrongly makes the plastic's light weight sound like the result.

g.passage: The bombardier beetle (Brachinus) defends itself in a remarkable way. When threatened, it mixes two chemicals stored separately in its abdomen inside a reinforced reaction chamber, a process that heats the mixture to nearly the boiling point of water ______ the beetle then sprays the scalding liquid at its attacker, aiming the stream by rotating the tip of its abdomen.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.design: 빈칸 앞 긴 동격 명사구(a process that heats...)가 독립절의 끝인지 판단해야 하며, 쉼표·접속사·관계사 오답이 각각 그럴듯하게 보이도록 구성했다.
g.explanation: "it mixes ... water"는 동격구 "a process that..."로 끝나는 독립절이고, "the beetle then sprays..."도 주어와 동사를 갖춘 독립절이다. 두 독립절은 세미콜론으로 연결할 수 있으므로 B가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 오용(comma splice)이 된다. C는 쉼표 없이 and로 연결해 동격구 안의 관계절 "that heats ..."에 이어지는 것처럼 읽혀 구조가 어색해지고, 독립절을 잇는 문장부호도 빠져 있다. D는 which가 관계대명사인데 뒤 절에 이미 주어(the beetle)와 목적어(the scalding liquid)가 모두 있어서 문법적으로 성립하지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: "It mixes ... water" is an independent clause that ends with the long appositive phrase "a process that...," and "the beetle then sprays..." is also an independent clause with its own subject and verb. A semicolon can correctly join two independent clauses, so B is correct. A joins the two clauses with only a comma, which creates a comma splice. C uses "and" without a comma, so the second clause reads as if it continues the relative clause "that heats ...," and there's still no proper punctuation joining the two independent clauses. D is wrong because "which" is a relative pronoun, but the clause after it already has a subject (the beetle) and an object (the scalding liquid), so it doesn't work grammatically.

g.passage: In Elena Varga's 2019 novel The Ashworth Lamps, the governess, a pale young woman who had arrived at the manor with a single trunk and a sealed letter of recommendation, rarely spoke at dinner______ when she did, the master of the house set down his fork and listened without interruption.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.design: 긴 동격 삽입구가 주절의 주어와 동사를 떼어 놓아서 첫 번째 독립절이 어디서 끝나는지 알아보기 어렵게 만들었다. 오답은 쉼표 이음(comma splice), 쉼표 없는 등위접속사, 융합문(run-on)으로 구성했다.
g.explanation: 긴 동격 삽입구를 걷어내면 'the governess rarely spoke at dinner'는 완전한 독립절이다. 빈칸 뒤 'when she did, the master ... listened'도 종속절을 앞에 둔 독립절이므로 두 절을 이어 주는 장치가 필요하다. C의 세미콜론은 접속사 없이 두 독립절을 바르게 연결하므로 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이은 쉼표 이음(comma splice)이고, D는 아무 문장부호도 없는 융합문이다. B는 'and'로 두 독립절을 잇지만 그 앞에 필요한 쉼표가 없어서, 'and when she did'가 앞 절에 붙은 것처럼 읽히는 어색한 구조가 된다.
g.explanation_en: If you strip away the long appositive, "the governess rarely spoke at dinner" is a complete independent clause. The part after the blank, "when she did, the master ... listened," is also an independent clause that opens with a dependent clause, so the two clauses need to be joined properly. Choice C uses a semicolon, which correctly joins two independent clauses without a conjunction, so C is the answer. Choice A joins the clauses with only a comma, which is a comma splice, and choice D uses no punctuation at all, which makes a run-on sentence. Choice B uses "and" but leaves out the comma that should come before a coordinating conjunction joining two independent clauses.

g.passage: Along the coast of Bangladesh, the Sundarbans mangrove forest acts as a living barrier against cyclones. g.explanation: "the researchers concluded"는 주어 "The reason"과 동사 "is" 사이에 끼어든 삽입구라서 앞뒤에 쉼표가 짝을 이뤄야 한다. 또 "is that" 뒤에는 that절이 보어로 바로 이어지므로 부호를 넣으면 안 된다. 따라서 D가 정답이다. A는 삽입구 쉼표는 맞지만 "that"과 그 절 사이에 불필요한 쉼표를 넣었다. B는 삽입구 뒤쪽 쉼표가 빠져 쌍을 이루지 못한다. C는 세미콜론이 "is that"과 그 보어 절을 떼어 놓아 앞부분이 완결되지 않은 문장이 된다.
g.explanation_en: "the researchers concluded" is an interrupting phrase between the subject "The reason" and the verb "is," so it has to be set off by a pair of commas. g.passage: In the 1840s, the Manchester cotton spinner and reformer Elena Hartwell (a composite figure used here for illustration) began collecting the wage books of local mills, documents that most historians of the period had dismissed as dull ledgers. Her persistence revealed a pattern that earlier accounts had ______ the hours recorded for children were often far longer than the limits set by the Factory Act of 1833.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "Her persistence revealed a pattern that earlier accounts had missed"는 완전한 독립절이고, 빈칸 뒤 "the hours recorded ... 1833"도 독립절이며 그 'pattern'이 무엇인지 구체적으로 설명한다. 콜론은 완전한 절 뒤에서 앞 내용을 풀어 설명하는 독립절을 이끌 수 있으므로 A가 정답이다. B는 쉼표 하나로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 연결 오류(comma splice)가 된다. C는 쉼표+and로 문법적으로는 이어지지만, 뒤 절을 앞 절의 'pattern'에 대한 설명이 아니라 별개의 추가 사실로 만들어 논리 관계가 흐려지고, 무엇보다 "missed"의 대상이 "pattern"이라는 구조와 어긋난다. g.explanation_en: The words before the blank, "Her persistence revealed a pattern that earlier accounts had missed," form a complete independent clause, and the words after the blank are also an independent clause that spells out what that "pattern" was. A colon can follow a complete clause to introduce an explanation of it, so A is correct. B joins two independent clauses with only a comma, which makes a comma splice. C is grammatical on the surface, but it turns the second clause into a separate added fact instead of the explanation of the "pattern," so the logic of the sentence falls apart. g.passage: In 2019, engineers at a Dutch water authority began testing a floating barrier designed to capture plastic waste in rivers before it reaches the sea. The device, a curved boom anchored at an angle to the current ______ debris toward a collection point on the riverbank, where crews can remove it without blocking boat traffic.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 "The device"이고, "a curved boom anchored at an angle to the current"는 주어를 다시 설명하는 동격 삽입구이다. 따라서 삽입구를 닫는 쉼표 뒤에 본동사 "guides"가 와야 하므로 B가 정답이다. A는 "and it"으로 새 절을 시작해 주어 "The device"가 본동사 없이 남게 된다. C의 세미콜론은 앞뒤에 완전한 독립절이 있어야 하는데, 앞부분에 본동사가 없고 뒷부분에는 주어가 없다. D의 "guiding"은 분사여서 본동사 역할을 할 수 없으므로 문장이 불완전해진다.
g.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is "The device," and "a curved boom anchored at an angle to the current" is an appositive that renames it. A comma has to close the appositive, and then the main verb "guides" follows, so B is correct. A starts a new clause with "and it," which leaves "The device" without a main verb. C uses a semicolon, which needs a complete independent clause on each side, but the first part has no main verb and the second part has no subject. D uses the participle "guiding," which can't serve as the main verb, so the sentence stays incomplete.
g.design: 긴 동격 삽입구(내부에 분사 수식어 포함) 뒤에서 본동사를 찾아야 하는 두 단계 판단이 필요하다. A와 D는 훑어 읽으면 그럴듯해 보이도록 오답으로 설계했다.

g.passage: The bdelloid rotifer, a microscopic freshwater animal that can survive complete drying out for years at a time, appears to have reproduced without sex for tens of millions of ______ it has picked up a substantial share of its genes from bacteria and fungi through a process known as horizontal gene transfer, which may supply some of the genetic variety that sex would otherwise provide.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 긴 동격구(a microscopic ... at a time)를 걸러 내면 주절 'The bdelloid rotifer ... appears to have reproduced ... years'와 독립절 'it has picked up ...'가 접속사 없이 이어진다. 'instead'는 접속부사이므로 두 절을 연결하려면 앞에 세미콜론이 필요하고, 뒤에는 쉼표를 둔다. 그래서 C가 정답이다. A와 D는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 comma splice가 된다(D는 instead 뒤 쉼표까지 빠졌다). B는 경계에 문장부호가 없어 run-on 문장이 된다.
g.explanation_en: Set aside the long appositive (a microscopic ... at a time), and you'll see the main clause "The bdelloid rotifer ... appears to have reproduced ... years" followed by a second independent clause, "it has picked up ...," with no conjunction between them. "Instead" is a conjunctive adverb, not a conjunction, so it needs a semicolon before it and a comma after it. That makes C the answer. A and D join two independent clauses with only a comma, which is a comma splice (D also drops the comma after "instead"). B puts no punctuation at the boundary, so it's a run-on sentence.
g.design: The clause boundary is hidden behind a long appositive, and the conjunctive adverb "instead" can be mistaken for a conjunction. The distractors use comma placements that each look partly reasonable.

Instead, she describes the objects her late husband left ______ a cracked pocket watch that still ticks, a ledger of unpaid debts, and a pair of boots she polishes every Sunday though no one will wear them again.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞은 "she describes the objects her late husband left behind"라는 완전한 독립절이고, 그 뒤에는 그 물건들을 구체적으로 나열하는 명사구가 온다. 완전한 절 뒤에 목록이나 설명을 붙일 때는 콜론을 쓰므로 D가 정답이다. g.explanation_en: The text before the blank, "she describes the objects her late husband left behind," is a complete independent clause. What follows is a noun-phrase list naming those objects. A colon is the right way to introduce a list or explanation after a complete clause, so D is correct. A is wrong because a semicolon needs an independent clause on both sides, and the second part here is only a list of noun phrases. B is wrong because "and" ends up joining the list to the clause even though there is no matching verb or clause to pair it with, which makes the sentence ungrammatical and illogical. C is wrong because it joins two independent clauses with only a comma, which creates a comma splice.

g.explanation: 빈칸 앞은 관계절(most of which ...)까지 포함한 하나의 독립절이고, 빈칸 뒤 'its waters ... never reach the coast'도 삽입구를 지나 동사 reach를 갖춘 독립절이다. 두 독립절은 세미콜론으로 연결해야 하므로 A가 정답이다. g.explanation: 긴 대시 삽입구를 걷어내면 "Its founders ... hoped the lectures would sharpen workers' practical skills"와 "many factory owners suspected ..."라는 두 독립절이 이어진다. 접속부사 however가 두 번째 절을 이끌므로 그 앞에 세미콜론, 뒤에 쉼표를 둔 B가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 콤마 스플라이스가 된다. C는 however를 첫 절에 붙여 의미상 대조가 엉뚱한 곳에 걸리고 두 번째 절과의 연결이 어색하다. D는 절 사이에 구두점이 없어 무종지문(run-on)이 된다.
g.explanation_en: If you set aside the long interruption between the dashes, you get two independent clauses: "Its founders ... hoped the lectures would sharpen workers' practical skills" and "many factory owners suspected ...". The conjunctive adverb "however" begins the second clause, so it needs a semicolon before it and a comma after it, which is choice B. Choice A joins the two independent clauses with only commas, which makes a comma splice. Choice C attaches "however" to the first clause, so the contrast lands in the wrong place and the clauses don't connect logically. Choice D has no punctuation between the clauses, which makes a run-on sentence.

g.passage: In 1978, structural engineer William LeMessurier discovered a serious flaw in New York's Citicorp Center, a 59-story tower he had helped design. The bolted joints in the tower's diagonal bracing, which a contractor had substituted for welded joints to reduce costs, ______ the building could buckle in a strong storm striking it diagonally. Crews secretly reinforced the joints at night over the following months.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: were too weak, the result was that
were too weak, and, as a result
g.design: 긴 비필수 관계절 뒤에서 주절의 동사를 찾은 다음, 그 뒤의 경계(절 vs 분사구)를 판단하게 했다. 오답은 각각 쉼표 오용, 접속사 뒤 구두점 오류, 세미콜론과 구를 잘못 결합한 경우로, 모두 부분적으로는 그럴듯하다.
g.explanation: 주어 "The bolted joints"는 쉼표 사이의 관계절을 건너뛴 뒤 동사 "were"와 연결되며, 빈칸 뒤 "the building could buckle..."는 완전한 절이다. C는 분사구 "meaning that"으로 뒤의 절을 that절로 이끌기 때문에 문법적으로 옳다. A는 두 독립절을 쉼표로만 잇는 쉼표 오류(comma splice)이다. B는 "as a result" 뒤에 쉼표가 없어 삽입구가 열리기만 하고 닫히지 않으므로 구두점이 맞지 않는다. D의 세미콜론 뒤에는 독립절이 와야 하는데, "meaning that..."은 독립절이 아닌 구이다.
g.explanation_en: The subject "The bolted joints" skips over the comma-enclosed relative clause and connects to the verb "were," and the words after the blank, "the building could buckle...," form a full clause. Choice C works because the participial phrase "meaning that" turns what follows into a that-clause, so the sentence is grammatical. Choice A joins two independent clauses with only a comma, which is a comma splice. Choice B opens an interrupting phrase with "and, as a result" but never closes it with a comma, so the punctuation is unbalanced. Choice D is wrong because a semicolon must be followed by an independent clause, and "meaning that..." is a phrase, not an independent clause.

g.passage: The mangrove rivulus, a small fish found in coastal swamps from Florida to Brazil, can survive out of water for weeks at a time. When its pools dry up, the fish wriggles into moist, rotting logs and absorbs oxygen through its skin______ researchers have found that during these dry spells its gills actually shrink, regrowing only after the fish returns to water.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.design: 빈칸 앞 'When...' 종속절과 주절, 뒤의 독립절 사이 경계를 판단해야 함. 오답 A·C는 부사 'remarkably'를 쉼표로 둘러 그럴듯해 보이지만 여전히 comma splice임.
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞 'When its pools dry up, the fish ... through its skin'은 완전한 독립절이고, 빈칸 뒤 'researchers have found ...'도 주어와 동사를 갖춘 독립절이다. 두 독립절은 마침표 등으로 분리해야 하므로, 마침표를 쓰고 'Remarkably,'로 새 문장을 시작하는 D가 정답이다. A는 'remarkably'를 쉼표로 감싸 삽입구처럼 보이게 했지만 접속사 없이 쉼표만으로 두 절을 잇는 comma splice이다. B도 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이은 comma splice이다. C는 'remarkably'가 앞 절의 'skin'을 꾸미는 것처럼 읽히고, 이 역시 쉼표만으로 두 절을 이은 comma splice이다.
g.explanation_en: The text before the blank, "When its pools dry up, the fish ... through its skin," is a complete independent clause, and "researchers have found ..." after the blank is also an independent clause with its own subject and verb. Two independent clauses must be properly separated, so D is correct: it ends the first sentence with a period and starts a new one with "Remarkably,". A sets off "remarkably" with commas so it looks like an interrupter, but it still joins two independent clauses with only commas, which is a comma splice. B is a plain comma splice. C makes "remarkably" seem attached to the first clause and still links the two clauses with just a comma, so it is also a comma splice.

g.passage: In Mara Ellison's novel The Lamplighter's Daughter, set in a fog-bound harbor town, the young governess Celia Vane discovers a packet of unsent letters hidden beneath the floorboards of her employer's study. The letters, written in a cramped and trembling ______ the true reason the household never speaks of the drowned elder son.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: "written in a cramped and trembling hand"는 주어 "The letters"와 동사 "reveal" 사이에 끼어든 비필수 삽입구이므로 앞뒤를 쉼표 한 쌍으로 묶어야 하고, 앞의 쉼표가 이미 있으니 뒤에도 쉼표가 필요하다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B는 닫는 쉼표가 빠져 삽입구가 동사까지 이어지는 것처럼 읽힌다. C의 세미콜론은 독립절 두 개를 잇는 부호인데, 세미콜론 앞부분은 동사가 없어 독립절이 아니며 주어와 동사를 갈라 놓는다. D는 "and"를 넣어 "reveal"이 주어와 연결될 주동사를 잃게 만들어, 문장에 주어 "The letters"의 동사가 없게 된다.
g.explanation_en: The phrase "written in a cramped and trembling hand" is a nonessential modifier that sits between the subject "The letters" and the verb "reveal," so it needs a pair of commas around it; since the opening comma is already there, you need a closing comma too. That makes A correct. B leaves out the closing comma, so the modifier seems to run right into the verb. C uses a semicolon, which should join two independent clauses, but the part before it has no main verb and isn't an independent clause, and the semicolon also cuts the subject off from its verb. D adds "and," which leaves "The letters" without a main verb, so the sentence never becomes a complete clause.
g.design: Making the student confirm that the subject's main verb comes after a long participial modifier means two steps are needed: closing the comma pair and checking that the clause is complete. B and D look natural if you skim, and C seems to mark a boundary.

g.passage: Most rivers eventually empty into an ocean, but the Okavango River ends far inland. The Okavango Delta—a vast wetland in northern Botswana where seasonal floodwaters fan out across the dry sands of the Kalahari Basin______ the sea; instead, nearly all of its water evaporates, is absorbed by plants, or seeps into the ground.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 주어 'The Okavango Delta' 뒤에 대시로 시작한 비필수 동격 삽입구가 'Basin'에서 끝나므로, 같은 대시로 닫은 뒤 본동사 'never reaches'로 이어져야 한다. 따라서 B가 정답이다. A는 대시로 연 삽입구를 쉼표로 닫아 부호 짝이 맞지 않는다. C의 세미콜론은 주어와 동사를 갈라놓아 앞부분을 동사 없는 불완전한 문장으로 만든다. D는 대시는 맞지만 'it'을 넣어 주어 'Delta'를 불필요하게 반복하므로 주어가 하나 남게 되고 문장이 성립하지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The subject "The Okavango Delta" is followed by a nonessential appositive. That appositive opens with a dash and ends at "Basin," so it must close with a matching dash before the main verb "never reaches." That makes B correct. A closes the dash-opened phrase with a comma, so the punctuation marks don't match. C uses a semicolon, which cuts the subject off from its verb and leaves the first part as a fragment with no verb. D uses the right dash but adds "it," which repeats the subject "Delta." That leaves "Delta" without a verb, so the sentence doesn't work.
g.design: The blank sits after a long appositive with an embedded "where" clause. Students have to find where the dash interruption ends and see that the main verb comes next. D is the best distractor because its dash is right, but adding "it" makes the sentence ungrammatical.

g.passage: In 1850, the British Parliament passed the Public Libraries Act, which allowed towns to fund free libraries through local taxes. Adoption was slow at first—many ratepayers objected to the added expense—but the idea gradually spread. Among the earliest adopters was Manchester, whose library opened in 1852 at a ceremony attended by the novelist Charles Dickens______ for the first time, the city's factory workers could borrow books without paying a subscription fee.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "Among the earliest adopters ... Charles Dickens"는 도치된 독립절이고, 빈칸 뒤 "for the first time, the city's factory workers could borrow books..."도 주어와 동사를 갖춘 독립절이다. 접속사 없이 두 독립절을 연결하려면 세미콜론이 필요하므로 C가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 오용(comma splice)이 된다. B의 "which"는 뒤에 이미 완전한 절이 있어 관계절이 성립하지 않는다. D는 아무 부호 없이 두 절을 붙인 무종지문(run-on)이다.
g.explanation_en: The text before the blank ("Among the earliest adopters ... Charles Dickens") is an inverted independent clause, and the text after it ("for the first time, the city's factory workers could borrow books...") is also an independent clause with its own subject and verb. When two independent clauses are joined without a conjunction, you need a semicolon, so C is correct. A joins the two clauses with only a comma, which creates a comma splice. B adds "which," but the clause that follows is already complete, so it can't work as a relative clause. D runs the two clauses together with no punctuation at all, which creates a run-on sentence.
g.design: 빈칸 앞 절은 도치 구조에 긴 수식어가 붙어 있고 빈칸 뒤 절은 도입 부사구로 시작해서, 두 절이 모두 독립절이라는 점을 훑어 읽기로는 놓치기 쉽다. 이 때문에 쉼표나 관계사 오답이 그럴듯해 보인다.

g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.design: 긴 비필수 관계절이 주절의 주어와 동사 사이에 끼어 있어 경계를 놓치기 쉽다. 학생은 앞부분 전체가 독립절임을 확인한 뒤, 뒤에 오는 독립절과의 연결 방식을 판단해야 한다.
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞의 'engineers ... realized that ... had calculated'는 삽입된 관계절을 지나 완결되는 독립절이고, 빈칸 뒤의 'welders spent ...'도 독립절이다. 두 독립절은 세미콜론으로 연결할 수 있으므로 D가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 오용(comma splice)이 된다. B는 쉼표+등위접속사 조합을 쓰려 했지만 and 뒤에 불필요한 쉼표가 들어가 있다. C는 쉼표 없이 and만으로 긴 독립절 두 개를 이어 표준 문장부호 관례에 어긋난다.
g.explanation_en: The text before the blank ("engineers ... realized that ... had calculated") is a complete independent clause once you read past the inserted relative clause, and "welders spent ..." is also an independent clause. A semicolon can join two independent clauses, so D is correct. A joins them with only a comma, which creates a comma splice. B tries to use a comma plus a coordinating conjunction but puts an extra comma after "and." C joins two long independent clauses with "and" and no comma, which doesn't follow standard punctuation conventions.

g.passage: The bdelloid rotifer, a microscopic freshwater animal that has reproduced without males for tens of millions of years, survives droughts by drying out completely and entering a dormant state. Biologist Chiara Boschetti found that during this process the rotifer's DNA shatters into fragments, yet the animal recovers when water ______ as it repairs its broken genome, it sometimes incorporates genes borrowed from bacteria and fungi.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "yet the animal recovers when water returns"와 뒤 "as it repairs ..., it sometimes incorporates ..."는 각각 독립절이므로 둘 사이에 세미콜론 같은 강한 경계가 필요하며, 접속부사 moreover는 뒤에 쉼표를 둔다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 이음(comma splice)이 된다. C는 세미콜론은 맞지만 moreover 뒤 쉼표가 없어, moreover가 "as it repairs"라는 종속절과 그대로 이어지므로 도입 부사가 분리되지 않는다. D는 두 독립절 사이에 아무 경계도 없어 무종지문(run-on)이 된다.
g.explanation_en: The words before the blank ("yet the animal recovers when water returns") and the words after it ("as it repairs its broken genome, it sometimes incorporates...") are both independent clauses, so they need a strong boundary such as a semicolon, and the conjunctive adverb "moreover" should be followed by a comma. That makes A correct. B joins two independent clauses with only commas, which creates a comma splice. C gets the semicolon right but leaves out the comma after "moreover," so the adverb runs straight into the dependent clause "as it repairs" without being set off. D puts no boundary at all between the two independent clauses, which makes it a run-on sentence.
g.design: The independent clause is long and opens with a dependent clause ("as it repairs..."), so you have to find where the clauses actually meet. The distractors each fix only part of the problem (a comma splice, a missing comma after the conjunctive adverb, and a run-on), so you have to compare them to rule them out.

g.design: 긴 동격구와 삽입구 때문에 주절 경계가 흐려지게 해, 빈칸 앞뒤가 각각 독립절임을 확인한 뒤 연결 방식을 판단하도록 했다. 오답은 접속사 뒤 쉼표, 세미콜론 뒤 종속절 등 부분적으로 그럴듯한 형태로 만들었다.
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞 'The lighthouse keeper's widow ... kept her shutters closed through the long autumn'과 빈칸 뒤 'only the lamp ... suggested ... that anyone lived in the house at all'은 둘 다 독립절이므로 세미콜론으로 연결한 B가 정답이다. g.explanation_en: The text before the blank ("The lighthouse keeper's widow ... kept her shutters closed through the long autumn") and the text after it ("only the lamp ... suggested ... that anyone lived in the house at all") are both independent clauses, so B is correct because a semicolon can join them. A uses only a comma to join two independent clauses, which creates a comma splice. C does use the coordinating conjunction "and," but the extra comma after "and" wrongly separates the conjunction from the subject "only the lamp." D puts "while" after the semicolon, which turns the second part into a dependent clause, and a semicolon has to be followed by an independent clause.

Each year, floodwaters that fell as rain in the Angolan highlands months earlier arrive during Botswana's dry ______ the delta swells to nearly three times its low-water size just when surrounding grasslands are at their most parched.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.design: 긴 수식절(that fell as rain... months earlier)이 붙은 주어 때문에 첫 절의 끝을 놓치기 쉽게 하고, 접속부사 as a result 앞의 경계 처리(세미콜론 vs 쉼표 연결)를 비교하게 했다. 오답 B는 등위접속사를 갖췄지만 쉼표 배치가 틀리게 해 비교가 필요하도록 했다.
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "floodwaters ... arrive during Botswana's dry season"은 독립절이고, 뒤의 "the delta swells ..."도 독립절이므로 두 절을 올바르게 이어야 한다. C는 세미콜론으로 두 독립절을 연결하고 접속부사 as a result 뒤에 쉼표를 두어 정답이다. g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "the programs sent women directly into crowded homes"는 독립절이고, 뒤의 "these women ... offered practical advice"도 독립절이므로 두 절 사이에 세미콜론 같은 경계가 필요하다. 또한 "many of whom ... served"는 비필수 삽입절이므로 앞뒤로 쉼표가 있어야 하는데, 뒤 쉼표는 이미 지문에 있으므로 "women" 뒤에도 쉼표가 필요하다. g.explanation_en: The text before the blank ("the programs sent women directly into crowded homes") is an independent clause, and "these women ... offered practical advice" is another independent clause, so you need a proper boundary like a semicolon between them. g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "The water ... carried fine glacial silt ... within months"는 독립절이고, 빈칸 뒤 "by the time the plant opened, the team had coated ..."도 주어(the team)와 동사(had coated)를 갖춘 독립절이다. 두 독립절은 세미콜론으로 연결할 수 있으므로 A가 정답이다. B는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 오용(comma splice)이 된다. C는 아무 부호 없이 두 절을 붙여 무종지문(run-on)이 된다. D는 등위접속사 and를 쓰긴 했지만 and 뒤에 불필요한 쉼표를 넣어 and와 "by the time" 구 사이를 부적절하게 끊는다.

The part after the blank, "by the time the plant opened, the team had coated ...," is also an independent clause, with the subject "the team" and the verb "had coated." A semicolon can correctly join two independent clauses, so A is correct. B joins them with only a comma, which creates a comma splice. C uses no punctuation at all, which creates a run-on sentence. D does use the conjunction "and," but the extra comma after "and" incorrectly separates the conjunction from the introductory phrase "by the time."

g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.design: 복수 주어 rates와 동사 사이에 단수 명사(explanation, interest)가 든 긴 삽입구를 넣어, 빈칸 바로 앞 명사에 수를 맞추는 오답(A, D)과 정동사가 없는 분사 오답(C)을 유도했다.
g.explanation: 콜론 뒤 절의 주어는 복수 명사 'rates'이고, 삽입구 'far more than ... sessions'를 건너뛰면 이 주어에 이어질 정동사가 필요하다. 따라서 복수 정동사인 B가 정답이다. A와 D는 정동사이긴 하지만 바로 앞의 단수 명사 'explanation'이나 'sessions' 근처의 'interest'에 수를 맞춘 단수형이라 복수 주어와 일치하지 않는다. C의 분사 'determining'은 정동사가 아니어서 콜론 뒤 절이 완전한 절이 되지 못한다.
g.explanation_en: The clause after the colon has the plural subject "rates," and once you skip the interrupting phrase "far more than ... sessions," that subject still needs a finite verb. B, the plural verb "determine," is the correct answer. A and D are finite verbs, but they are singular. They match the nearby singular noun "explanation" (or "interest"), not the actual plural subject. C, "determining," is a participle rather than a finite verb, so the clause after the colon would be left without a main verb.

g.design: The singular subject "The version" is separated from the verb by an "along with" phrase containing plural nouns, so students must find the real subject and also see that the sentence needs a finite verb.
g.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 단수 명사 "The version"이다. "along with ~ tones"는 삽입된 수식어구일 뿐이라 주어를 복수로 만들지 않는다. 또한 이 문장에는 정동사가 따로 없으므로 빈칸에 단수 정동사가 들어가야 한다. 따라서 C "is"가 정답이다. A "are"와 B "have been"은 정동사이긴 하지만 바로 앞의 "terms", "names", "tones"에 이끌린 복수형이어서 단수 주어와 맞지 않는다. D "being"은 분사여서 정동사가 아니므로 완전한 문장이 되지 않는다.

The sentence also has no other main verb, so the blank needs a singular finite verb. That makes C, "is," the answer. g.passage: The collection of more than 500 pressed specimens that Mexican American botanist Ynés Mexía gathered during her expeditions through Mexico, Brazil, and Peru in the 1920s and 1930s ______ now stored at several herbaria, where researchers consult it to track how plant ranges have shifted over the past century.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 단수 명사 "The collection"이며, "of more than 500 pressed specimens"와 "that ... 1930s" 관계절은 이를 꾸미는 수식어일 뿐이다. 따라서 빈칸에는 단수 주어와 일치하는 정동사가 필요하고, "now"가 현재를 가리키므로 A가 정답이다. B는 시제는 맞지만 바로 앞의 복수 명사(specimens, the 1920s and 1930s)에 잘못 일치시킨 복수형이다. C와 D는 분사 형태로 정동사가 아니므로, 주절에 본동사가 없는 불완전한 문장이 된다.
g.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is the singular noun "The collection." The phrase "of more than 500 pressed specimens" and the relative clause "that ... 1930s" only modify it. That means the blank needs a finite verb that agrees with a singular subject, and "now" calls for the present tense, so A is correct. B uses the right tense, but it's plural, so it wrongly agrees with nearby plural nouns like "specimens." C and D are participles, not finite verbs, so either one would leave the main clause without a main verb and make the sentence a fragment.
g.design: This item tests agreement between a singular subject and its verb after a long prepositional phrase and relative clause that are full of plural nouns, along with the difference between finite verbs and participles. A quick reader may choose B or C, so the reader has to find the true subject and also confirm that the sentence needs a finite verb.

g.passage: Unlike most planetary nebulae, which glow for only a few tens of thousands of years before fading, the faint shell of gas surrounding the white dwarf known to astronomers as Sh 2-188 ______ unusually lopsided, its brighter edge compressed as the star plows through the surrounding interstellar medium.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 'the faint shell'(단수)이고, 'of gas surrounding the white dwarf known to astronomers as Sh 2-188'은 이를 꾸미는 수식어구일 뿐이므로 빈칸에는 단수 정동사가 와야 한다. 따라서 B 'appears'가 정답이다. A 'appearing'과 D 'to appear'는 정동사가 아니라서 문장에 본동사가 없게 된다. C 'appear'는 정동사이긴 하지만 복수형이다. 바로 앞의 'planetary nebulae'나 'tens of thousands of years'에 수를 맞춘 형태라 주어와 일치하지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is "the faint shell," which is singular. The phrase "of gas surrounding the white dwarf known to astronomers as Sh 2-188" only modifies it, so the blank needs a singular finite verb, and that makes B, "appears," correct. A ("appearing") and D ("to appear") aren't finite verbs, so with either one the sentence would have no main verb. C ("appear") is a finite verb, but it's plural. It matches nearby plural nouns like "planetary nebulae" or "years" instead of the actual subject.

g.passage: In a field study of bus commuters, behavioral economist Rosa Quispe examined how default settings on prepaid transit cards influenced riders' choices. Each new card was automatically enrolled in a monthly payment plan unless the rider actively selected a different one. Quispe found that the proportion of riders who stayed on that automatic plan through the full twelve months of the study ______ nearly 80 percent, even though cheaper alternatives were clearly advertised at every station.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 이 절의 주어는 단수 명사 'the proportion'이며, 'of riders who stayed on that automatic plan through the full twelve months of the study'는 주어와 동사 사이에 끼어든 수식어구이다. 따라서 단수 동사가 필요하고, 'found', 'were clearly advertised'처럼 과거 시제로 서술된 완료된 연구이므로 과거형 'was'(C)가 맞다. A의 'were'는 시제는 맞지만 가까이 있는 복수 명사 'riders'나 'months'에 수를 맞춘 복수형이다. B의 'are'는 복수형인 데다 현재 시제이다. D의 'have been'도 복수형이며, 현재완료는 끝난 연구를 서술하는 과거 시제 문맥과 맞지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The subject of this clause is the singular noun "the proportion." The phrase "of riders who stayed on that automatic plan through the full twelve months of the study" is a modifier that sits between the subject and the verb. That means you need a singular verb, and because the passage describes a finished study in the past tense ("found," "were clearly advertised"), the past-tense "was" in C is correct. A has the right tense, but "were" is plural, so it matches the nearby plural nouns "riders" or "months" instead of the real subject. B is plural and also in the present tense. D is plural too, and the present perfect doesn't fit the past-tense account of a completed study.
g.design: A long prepositional phrase and relative clause with plural nouns sit between the singular subject and the verb. The answer also requires checking the tense, so you have to make two judgments: number and tense.

g.passage: For decades, researchers interested in how Mongolian herding communities name colors, winds, and horse markings had to travel to a single library in Ulaanbaatar to consult the original sources. That changed recently: the archive of handwritten field notebooks compiled by anthropologists working among herders in the country's northern provinces during the 1960s ______ fully digitized, allowing scholars anywhere to search its thousands of vocabulary entries.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 단수 명사 'the archive'이고, 'of handwritten field notebooks ... during the 1960s'는 주어를 꾸미는 긴 수식어구이므로 단수 정동사가 필요하다. D의 'has been'은 단수형이고, 'changed recently'와 'allowing scholars anywhere'가 가리키는 최근 완료된 결과와도 맞는다. A는 완료 시제는 맞지만 'notebooks'나 'anthropologists'에 잘못 일치시킨 복수형이다. B 역시 복수형이라 단수 주어와 맞지 않는다. C는 분사라서 콜론 뒤 절에 정동사가 없게 된다.
g.explanation_en: The subject of this clause is the singular noun "the archive." Everything from "of handwritten field notebooks" through "during the 1960s" is a long modifier describing that subject, so you need a singular finite verb. D, "has been," is singular, and it also fits the context: "That changed recently" and "allowing scholars anywhere" point to a recently completed result. A uses the right perfect tense, but it's plural, as if the verb agreed with "notebooks" or "anthropologists." B is plural too, so it doesn't agree with the singular subject. C is a participle, which would leave the clause after the colon with no main verb.

g.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is the plural noun "rooms." After the clause "which ... treetops," the sentence still needs a main verb. g.passage: Magnetars, a rare class of neutron stars, possess magnetic fields roughly a thousand times stronger than those of ordinary neutron stars. According to astrophysicist Ersin Göğüş, the sudden bursts of X-rays that these objects occasionally emit, which can release more energy in a fraction of a second than the Sun does in thousands of years, ______ from fractures in the star's rigid outer crust.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.design: 문장의 주어 'bursts'와 빈칸 사이에 관계절 두 개를 넣고, 빈칸 바로 앞에 단수 명사(energy, Sun, years 근처 'does')를 두어 수 일치를 헷갈리게 했다. 동시에 비정동사 선택지를 섞어 두 단계 판단이 필요하도록 만들었다.

A and D are finite verbs, but they are singular ("originates," "is"), and the singular phrase "the Sun does" right before the blank makes them easy to choose by mistake. g.passage: In a 2019 field study of rideshare drivers in three Latin American cities, economist Paula Herrera examined how drivers respond to unexpectedly high earnings early in a shift. Standard labor models predict that drivers should keep working when hourly pay is high. However, the set of drivers who reached their usual daily earnings well before the end of a typical shift, especially those who had set an explicit income target at the start of the week, ______ more likely than other drivers to log off early, a pattern consistent with "reference-dependent" preferences.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 단수 명사 "the set"이고, "of rideshare drivers ... week"는 그 사이에 끼어든 긴 수식어구이다. 따라서 문장에는 단수 정동사가 필요하므로 D "was"가 정답이다. A "were"와 C "have been"은 빈칸 바로 앞의 복수 명사(drivers, those)에 동사를 잘못 일치시킨 선택지이다. 특히 C는 시제 측면에서 그럴듯해 보이지만 복수형이다. B "being"은 분사이므로 문장에 필요한 정동사 역할을 할 수 없다.

The sentence therefore needs a singular finite verb, so D, "was," is correct. g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.design: 수식어구가 길어서 주어 'A series'와 동사 사이에 복수 명사(vessels, techniques, workshops)가 끼어 있다. 그래서 수 일치를 판단하고 'since last spring'으로 시제까지 확인하는 두 단계 판단이 필요하다.
g.explanation: 문장의 주어는 단수 명사 'A series'이고, 'of glazed vessels that ... workshops'는 이 주어를 꾸미는 수식어구다. 또한 'since last spring'은 과거에 시작돼 현재까지 이어지는 상태를 나타내므로 현재완료 단수형이 필요하다. 따라서 D가 정답이다. A는 현재완료 시제는 맞지만, 가까운 복수 명사에 맞춰 복수형을 써서 주어와 수가 일치하지 않는다. B는 단순과거라서 'since'와 함께 쓸 수 없다. C는 분사이므로 문장에 정동사가 없게 된다.
g.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is the singular noun "A series." The words "of glazed vessels that ... workshops" form a long modifier that comes between that subject and its verb. The phrase "since last spring" describes a situation that started in the past and is still going on, so you need a singular present perfect verb. That makes D correct. A uses the right tense, but it is plural, which means it agrees with the nearby plural nouns instead of the real subject. B is simple past, which doesn't work with "since," and C is a participle, so the sentence would be left without a main verb.

- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.

g.passage: Astronomers studying the globular cluster Omega Centauri have long puzzled over its unusually broad range of stellar ages. According to a 2023 analysis led by astrophysicist Maximilian Häberle, the motions of seven fast-moving stars near the cluster's core, which were tracked across more than two decades of Hubble Space Telescope images, ______ the presence of an intermediate-mass black hole roughly 8,200 times as massive as the Sun.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 빈칸이 들어 있는 절의 주어는 "the motions"(복수)이고, 그 뒤의 "of seven fast-moving stars near the cluster's core"와 which 관계절은 주어를 꾸미는 수식어일 뿐이다. 따라서 이 절에는 복수 주어에 맞는 정동사가 필요하므로 A가 정답이다. B는 정동사이긴 하지만 바로 앞의 "core"나 "images"가 아니라 가까운 단수 명사 "core"에 끌려 단수로 맞춘 형태라서 복수 주어 motions와 수가 일치하지 않는다. C와 D는 분사 형태라 정동사 역할을 못 하므로 문장에 본동사가 없는 불완전한 문장이 된다.
g.explanation_en: The subject of this clause is "the motions," which is plural. The phrase "of seven fast-moving stars near the cluster's core" and the "which" clause after it only modify that subject. So the clause needs a finite verb that agrees with a plural subject, and that makes A correct. B is a finite verb, but it's singular. It agrees with a nearby singular noun like "core" instead of the real subject, "motions." C and D are participles, so they can't work as the main verb, and the sentence would be left without one.
g.design: 긴 전치사구와 관계절을 주어와 동사 사이에 넣어 주어-동사 거리를 늘렸고, 단수 명사 core를 가까이 두어 B를 유혹 오답으로 만들었다. C와 D는 정동사가 필요하다는 점을 확인하지 못하면 고를 수 있는 분사 오답이다.

g.passage: In a field study at a mid-sized logistics firm, behavioral economist Mette Lindqvist examined how default settings shape employees' saving decisions. The proportion of workers who remained enrolled in the company's retirement plan after the firm switched from opt-in to automatic enrollment ______ sharply, rising from roughly 41 percent to nearly 88 percent within a single year.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 'workers'나 'plan'이 아니라 단수 명사 'The proportion'이므로 단수 동사가 필요하다. 또 이 문장에는 정동사가 따로 없고, 연구는 과거에 일어난 일이므로 과거시제 정동사인 B가 정답이다. A는 과거시제지만 복수형이라 바로 앞의 'workers'에 잘못 일치시킨 것이다. C도 복수형인 데다 현재완료여서 'within a single year'라는 과거의 일과 어울리지 않는다. D는 분사일 뿐이어서 문장에 정동사가 없게 된다.
g.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is the singular noun "The proportion," not "workers" or "plan," so the verb must be singular. The sentence also has no other main verb, and the study describes a finished past event, so the past-tense main verb in B is correct. A is in the past tense, but it is plural, so it wrongly agrees with the nearby noun "workers." C is also plural, and its present perfect form doesn't fit a change that is over and was measured "within a single year." D is only a participle, so it would leave the sentence without a main verb.
g.design: 긴 관계절·전치사구가 주어 proportion과 동사를 떼어 놓아, 수 일치와 정동사 여부를 함께 판단해야 한다. 일부 오답은 시제나 수 가운데 한 가지만 맞도록 만들었다.

g.passage: The collection of whistled-speech recordings that linguist Julien Meyer and his colleagues gathered in mountain villages across the Canary Islands, northern Turkey, and Oaxaca, Mexico, ______ researchers to compare how different communities convert spoken vowels into distinct pitch contours.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 단수 명사 "collection"이고, "of whistled-speech recordings that ... Mexico"는 이 주어를 꾸미는 긴 수식어구이다. 따라서 빈칸에는 단수 주어와 일치하는 정동사가 필요하므로 C가 정답이다. A와 D는 수식어구 안의 복수 명사 "recordings"(또는 "colleagues", "villages")에 수를 맞춘 복수 동사이므로 주어와 일치하지 않는다. B는 분사이기 때문에 문장에 정동사가 없게 되어 완전한 문장이 되지 못한다.
g.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is the singular noun "collection." The long phrase "of whistled-speech recordings that ... Mexico" only describes that subject. So the blank needs a finite verb that agrees with a singular subject, and that makes C correct. A and D are plural verbs. They agree with the nearby plural nouns inside the modifier ("recordings," "colleagues," "villages") instead of with the actual subject. B is a participle, so it leaves the sentence without a main verb, and the result is a fragment.
g.design: A long modifier full of plural nouns separates the singular subject from the verb. Two options are plural traps, and one tests whether the sentence has a main verb, so students must find the subject and also confirm that a finite verb is needed.

g.passage: In her 1986 conversion of a former drum factory in São Paulo, architect Lina Bo Bardi added two raw concrete towers beside the old brick sheds. Critics often single out one feature of the design. The angular openings punched into the walls of the taller tower, which Bo Bardi described as resembling caves and left deliberately unglazed so that breezes could pass through the gymnasium floors, ______ the building an unfinished, almost archaeological character.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 복수형인 'The angular openings'이며, 'which ... floors'는 주어를 꾸미는 긴 관계절이다. 따라서 빈칸에는 복수 주어와 수가 일치하는 정동사가 와야 하므로 D 'give'가 정답이다. A 'gives'와 C 'has given'은 정동사라는 점은 맞지만 단수형이어서, 빈칸 바로 앞의 'tower'나 'floors' 근처 명사에 이끌린 오류다. B 'giving'은 분사여서 문장에 본동사가 없게 되므로 문장이 완성되지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is the plural noun phrase "The angular openings." The long "which" clause is only a modifier between the subject and the verb. So the blank needs a finite verb that agrees with a plural subject, which makes D, "give," correct. A ("gives") and C ("has given") are finite verbs, but they are singular, so they don't agree with "openings." They tempt you because of the singular nouns nearby, such as "tower." B ("giving") is a participle, so the sentence would be left without a main verb.
g.design: The plural subject and its verb are separated by a long relative clause full of singular nouns. To answer, the student has to make two judgments: whether a finite verb is needed and whether that verb agrees in number with the subject.

g.passage: In 1947, sculptor Ruth Asawa traveled to Toluca, Mexico, where local artisans taught her a looped-wire technique used to make egg baskets. The suspended wire forms that she went on to create with this technique, now exhibited in museums from San Francisco to New York, ______ light in such a way that each sculpture casts layered shadows that seem to double it on the surrounding walls.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 복수 명사 'forms'이다. 관계절 'that she went on to create with this technique'와 분사구 'now exhibited in museums...'는 주어를 꾸미는 수식어일 뿐이고, 문장에는 아직 본동사가 없다. 따라서 복수 주어와 수가 일치하는 정동사 A(catch)가 들어가야 한다. B와 D는 정동사이지만 단수형이어서, 빈칸 가까이에 있는 'technique'나 'New York'을 주어로 잘못 본 경우에 고르게 된다. C는 분사이므로 문장에 본동사가 없는 비문이 된다.
g.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is the plural noun "forms." The relative clause "that she went on to create with this technique" and the phrase "now exhibited in museums..." only modify that subject, so the sentence still needs a main verb. Choice A, "catch," is a finite verb that agrees with the plural subject, so it is correct. Choices B and D are finite verbs, but they are singular, so they would only work if you mistook a nearby noun such as "technique" or "New York" for the subject. Choice C is a participle, which would leave the sentence without a main verb.
g.design: 이 문항은 두 단계 판단을 요구한다. 학생은 긴 관계절과 분사구 뒤에 숨은 복수 주어를 찾아야 하고, 문장에 본동사가 없다는 점도 확인해야 한다. 오답 두 개는 단수 정동사로 배치해 빈칸 가까이에 있는 명사에 끌린 학생이 고르도록 했고, 나머지 오답 하나는 앞의 분사 'exhibited'와 이어지는 것처럼 보이는 분사로 구성했다.

g.passage: In 1974, astronomers Russell Hulse and Joseph Taylor discovered a pulsar locked in a tight orbit with a companion neutron star. Over the following decades, precise timing of the pulsar's radio pulses revealed that the orbit of the two dense stars, each packing more mass than the Sun into a sphere only about 20 kilometers across, ______ by roughly 3.5 meters per year, exactly the rate predicted if the system were losing energy through gravitational waves.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: that절의 주어는 단수 명사 "the orbit"이고, "of the two dense stars"와 삽입된 긴 수식어구는 주어를 꾸밀 뿐이므로 절에는 단수 정동사가 필요하다. 따라서 B "was shrinking"이 정답이다. A는 정동사이긴 하지만 바로 앞의 복수 명사 "stars"에 수를 맞춘 것이라 단수 주어 "orbit"과 일치하지 않는다. C와 D는 분사형이라 정동사 역할을 할 수 없어 that절이 동사 없는 불완전한 절이 된다.
g.explanation_en: The subject of the "that" clause is the singular noun "the orbit." The phrase "of the two dense stars" and the long modifier set off by commas only describe that subject, so the clause needs a singular finite verb. That makes B, "was shrinking," correct. A is a finite verb, but it agrees with the nearby plural noun "stars" rather than with "orbit." C and D are participles, so neither can work as the main verb, and either one would leave the "that" clause without a verb.
g.design: 긴 전치사구와 삽입 수식어로 단수 주어와 동사를 떼어 놓고, 복수 명사 "stars" 쪽으로 끌리는 오답을 넣었다. 그래서 학생은 동사가 정동사여야 하는지와 주어에 수가 맞는지를 둘 다 판단해야 한다.
